## Summary

**CMPIW** (Compare Immediate Word extended Long): Subtract & use only the condition.

## Details

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Operation | `<ea> – data → cc` |
| Syntax | `CMPIW.L #<data>,<ea>` |
| Short | Subtract & use only the condition. |
| Description | Sign extend immediate word data to long, subtract it from the destination and sets the condition codes according to the result. Size is long. |
| Condition codes | see table |

### Condition codes

| X | N | Z | V | C |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| – | * | * | * | * |

### Encoding

| Word | Bits | Content |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 15–6 | `0100111000` |
| 1 | 5–3 | Mode |
| 1 | 2–0 | Register |
| 2 | 15–0 | 16-bit word data |

### Notes

- There is no subiw.l

## Differences from AmigaOS / AROS / 68060

- The 68000–68060 have no CMPIW. It is new on the 68080.

## Do / Don't

- DON'T look for SUBIW.L: it does not exist.
